annotations.shape: one text/plain us-ascii message whose Date offset token is +9960 -- outside the design's +/-9959 limit; the offset token is kept as stated and the instant is unknown
annotations.raw_fixture: hand-written bytes in tools/write_raw_fixtures.py, frozen in fixtures/raw/SHA256SUMS -- the generator's pinned dates all carry a legal offset
annotations.phase_0_facts: container.*, headers.fields, part.tree, part.regions, part.gaps, body.preamble_epilogue, decode.chain and body.content_sha256
annotations.phase_1_facts: headers.date: the zone state stays zone_stated (a token is present) and the offset column keeps '+9960', but the UTC instant cannot be trusted, so utc is ['unknown', 'headers.invalid_date']
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes with a hex-editor-style line dump and typed by a model from the RFC and design rules (D2, RFC 5322 3.3), never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: a field's raw_span covers its line including the line ending; value_span starts immediately after the colon and keeps the leading space
annotations.expected_gaps: none at phase 0; the design names no registry id for an out-of-range offset, so the date is recorded as invalid through its utc reason and no new gap id is invented
annotations.not_yet_labelled: addresses, encoded words, body views, attachments, statuses, thread edges and TimeEvents

value: the design fixes the +/-9959 offset limit and says an invalid date sorts at a named end, but does not say whether an out-of-range offset keeps zone_state 'zone_stated' or becomes 'zone_absent'; zone_stated with the token kept is typed here
